text:
Predicates:
Nice(x, y) ::: x is nice to y.
Mean(x, y) ::: x is mean to y.
Grumpy(x) ::: x is a grumpy person.
AnimalLover(x) ::: x is an animal lover.
PetOwner(x) ::: x is a pet owner.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Nice(x, y) → ¬Mean(x, y)) ::: No one nice to animals is also mean to animals.
∃x (Grumpy(x) ∧ Mean(x, animals)) ::: Some grumpy people are mean to animals.
∀x (AnimalLover(x) → Nice(x, animals)) ::: All animal lovers are nice to animals.
∀x (PetOwner(x) → AnimalLover(x)) ::: All pet owners love animals.
PetOwner(tom) ::: Tom is a pet owner.
Conclusion:
¬(Grumpy(tom) ∧ Mean(tom, animals)) → ¬(Grumpy(tom) ∨ AnimalLover(tom)) ::: If Tom is not both a grumpy person and mean to animals, then Tom is neither a grumpy person nor an animal lover.
